title: Candidate 48 has no full U(2) multiplicity gauge symmetry to remove the second-vector data

claim.statement: Admissible gauge transformations quotient at most two of candidate 48's five exact moduli at generic points, leaving three physical flat directions; the independent eta circle is not gauge.
claim.implication: The corrected second vector-5 multiplicity cannot be dismissed as a pure U(2) gauge redundancy using the established candidate gauge algebra.

interpretation: The U(2) parameterization of the vacuum family is larger than the actual admissible gauge orbit.
At generic points two U(2)-type tangent combinations are gauge, while two further U(2)-type combinations plus eta remain physical.
Because v655's rank-six half-scalar/half-vector invariants persist over the whole family, gauge quotienting cannot reveal a hidden compensator point.
A new multiplicity gauge symmetry would have to be added and checked for anomalies/dynamics rather than inferred from the existing flat family.
falsifiers: An enlarged admissible gauge algebra acting on the completed module could alter the quotient and must be explicitly constructed.
The audit is local in moduli space; global discrete identifications can further quotient but cannot remove continuous local dimensions.
The link to the vector-copy issue is dimensional and structural, not a direct identification of every physical modulus with relative vector orientation.
nextBranches: Test whether the full 168-dimensional completed module admits an enlarged multiplicity gauge algebra compatible with the scalar ansatz.
Construct explicit V2=cV1 constraints and check whether they are first- or second-class.
Treat the remaining three moduli as physical fields and compute their coupling to the proposed gravitational connection.

evidence.note: Existing gauge-quotient computation reinterpreted after the corrected 2x5 carrier decomposition.
